title: Echopoint gate red on network resets: its transport reruns reused one idempotency key and got 409
summary: On 2026-11-16 at 20:53Z the echopoint post-deploy gate on dev lost 4 of 65 flows to TCP resets between the 1340p runner and the Cloudflare edge. The gate reruns such flows once, but each rerun was a single-flow `echopoint flows run` in the same step, and the CLI derived one idempotency key per job attempt for all of them: the first rerun passed, the other three got 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT`, and the gate went red. A manual job rerun passed at 21:02Z. Prod was not held, because the deploy was a redeploy of the image prod already ran. Two reset cleanups leaked throwaway Anchor orgs on dev for 3 h 18 min, until this routine deleted them. echopoint-cli#106 (v4.1.1) and ci-workflows#53 give every launch its own key; the routine now reads every gate attempt for leaks.

impact.text: Dev and CI only. The red gate fired the deploy failure alert and needed a manual job rerun (9 min red). Prod was not held: the redeploy was of `sha-829f4b1`, already on prod since 16:50Z. Two throwaway Anchor organizations stayed on the dev Nanostack product for 3 h 18 min.

numbers.label: gate red until the manual rerun passed
two leaked dev orgs before deletion

trigger: TCP resets from the 1340p runner (192.168.2.18) to the Cloudflare edge (172.64.80.1) failed 4 flows at once in the echopoint gate; the gate's rerun step then relaunched 4 single flows under one derived idempotency key.
detection: The gate job failed at 20:54:22Z and its `alert-deploy-failure` job ran at 20:54:24Z, so detection took 27 s from the first failed flow. The two `TRANSPORT-LEAK` warnings were seen by nobody: the gate only reports them, and its replacement attempt 2 hid attempt 1 from the run's job list. This routine found them at 00:10Z by reading attempt 1's log.
resolution: A human reran the failed job at 20:59:31Z; attempt 2 passed all flows at 21:02:46Z. echopoint-cli#106 (derive the key per step and per flow, released v4.1.1, Action `v1` now v4.2.0) and ci-workflows#53 (explicit `transport-rerun-<run>-<attempt>-<flow>` key) removed the cause by 22:26Z. The routine deleted both leaked orgs at 00:12Z, verified the fix live at 00:20Z, and added a gate-log scan to `run_suites.sh`.

whys.problem: The echopoint post-deploy gate went red on network resets it is built to rerun, and two throwaway orgs leaked on dev

because.text: Three of the four transport reruns were refused with 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT, so the gate counted them as failures
because.evidence: Gate log 20:54:20-21Z: `launch flow: unexpected status 409 … Idempotency key reused with different launch parameters`, then `failed again on its rerun`

because.text: Each rerun was a single-flow `flows run` in one step, and the CLI sent the same derived key for every one of them
because.evidence: echopoint-cli#106: `deriveGitHubIdempotencyKey(flowIDs)` ignored its argument; `executeFlows` sent the base key unchanged for one flow

because.text: The CLI's Actions key named the job attempt, not the launch it guards (flow, step), and no test ran two single-flow runs in one job
because.evidence: Behaviour since the CLI was first published (echopoint-cli#106 body); its new tests fail on the old derivation

because.text: Nobody saw the conflict in the 10 days since the rerun step shipped
because.evidence: The routine's run log records gate reruns of one flow each (2026-11-12, 2026-11-16 anchor); one rerun takes the free job key and passes

because.text: The gate's rerun step has no test that drives it; it is checked only by live failures, and both its PRs say 'not exercised live'
because.evidence: ci-workflows#42 and #53 Verification sections; the SAMPLES self-test checks only which errors count as transport

because.text: Four flows failed at the same moment on resets to the Cloudflare edge
because.evidence: `read tcp 192.168.2.18:* -> 172.64.80.1:443: connection reset by peer`, 20:52:07Z (anchor gate) to 20:53:57Z, during anchor and echopoint deploys

because.text: The 1340p → Cloudflare path resets connections in bursts, and the gate runs on that path
because.evidence: Same resets in the 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-13 gate postmortems

because.text: The reset class has no owner: the path investigation actions of the 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-13 postmortems are still open
Two throwaway orgs stayed on the dev product for 3 h 18 min after the gate named their cleanup nodes
because.evidence: Routine temp flows 00:12Z: GET 200, DELETE 204, GET 404 for `org_3MClO1WQ…` and `org_3MClFtjs…`

because.text: The gate only warns TRANSPORT-LEAK, and the green attempt 2 replaced attempt 1 in the run's job list
No one owns a gate leak between routine runs, and no sweep deletes throwaway orgs that outlive their run
because.evidence: Sweep action A5 of the 2026-10-21 transport postmortem is still open; the session that reran and fixed the gate left the leaks

contributing: The redeploy at 20:50Z ran together with anchor dev+prod deploys and an echopoint prod redeploy (20:49-20:57Z) on the same host path.
The fix session wrote no ledger row or postmortem, so the leaks and the 409 were not linked until the next routine run.

well: Another session found the 409, fixed both the CLI and the gate with tests, and shipped both within 1 h 32 min of the red gate.
The gate's TRANSPORT-LEAK lines named the exact flow and node, so the leaked orgs were easy to find and delete.
wrong: The leaks waited for the next routine run, because the gate reports leaks but nobody acts on them in between.
The rerun step shipped on 2026-11-06 with no test of its launch path, only of its error classification.
lucky: The redeploy carried the image prod already ran; on a feature merge, prod would have been held until a human reran the job.
The 409 refused the launch before any execution, so no rerun replayed or duplicated a side effect.
The leaked orgs were throwaway orgs on the shared dev product; a reset DELETE of a shared fixture would have left a real one half-deleted.

actions.what: Derive the Actions idempotency key per step and per flow; tests for two flows in one step and one flow in two steps
Gate reruns pass an explicit transport-rerun-<run>-<attempt>-<flow> key
A dispatchable self-test of echopoint-test.yml that forces two or more transport reruns (stub CLI or a flow that resets) and asserts each relaunches
run_suites.sh reads every Deploy Router gate attempt since the last run and prints GATE-TRANSPORT-LEAK and GATE-RERUN-REFUSED lines
Sweep throwaway Anchor orgs and product users on the shared dev product that outlive their run by more than 1 h
flow-suite-testing skill: give every CI rerun its own idempotency key; whoever reruns a gate deletes its TRANSPORT-LEAK resources
Own the 1340p → Cloudflare reset investigation (A4/A5 of the 2026-11-13 postmortem)

messaging.internal: Echopoint dev gate went red on 2026-11-16 20:54Z: 4 flows lost to TCP resets, and 3 of the 4 reruns were refused (409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT) because the CLI reused one key per job. Rerun passed 21:02Z; prod unaffected. Fixed by echopoint-cli#106 and ci-workflows#53. Two leaked dev orgs deleted 2026-11-17 00:12Z.
